summary: Andrew Glass works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at Bukkyo University and the University of Washington (MA 2000, PhD 2006 under Richard Salomon), as well as under Mark Allon, Ulrich Pagel, Sonam Wanggyal, and Gudrun Melzer.
Andrew J. Nicholson specializes in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied under traditional teacher Shree Narayan Mishra and holds a post at Stony Brook University.

Andrew Olendzki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Lancaster University. He served as executive director at the Insight Meditation Society, Executive Director and Resident Scholar at Barre Center for Buddhist Studies (attested 2003-2014), and senior scholar at Mind & Life Institute (attested 2014).

Andrew P. Tuck specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Princeton University and was taught by Victor Preller, Jeffrey Stout, William E. Kennick, Robert A. F. Thurman, John Pemberton, D. Dennis Hudson, Daniel H. H. Ingalls, Alan Sponberg, and Richard Rorty.
Andrew Quintman works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Jay L. Garfield and served as assistant professor in the Department of Religious Studies at Yale University (attested 2015).
Andrew William Kennedy specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Leeds (attested 2006) under the doctoral supervision of Philip A. Mellor and Kim Knott.

Andrey Klebanov works in Indology and linguistics. He earned his MA (2010) and PhD (2016) at the University of Hamburg under doctoral supervisors Harunaga Isaacson and Dominic Goodall. Attested as a professor at Kyoto University in 2019, he taught Kenji Takahashi.

Andrey Terentyev is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University's Faculty of Philosophy (~1969-1975) and worked at the Museum of History of Religion (~1978-1993). He also taught Ming Mei.

Andrzej Gawroński (1885-1927) was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Lviv University (~1902-1903) and Leipzig University (~1903-1907), and later held posts at Jagiellonian University (~1912-1916) and Lviv University (~1916-1927).

András Róna-Tas is a scholar of linguistics, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University (1950-1955), served as a guest lecturer at the University of Vienna (1983-1984), and presided over the International Association for Tibetan Studies (~1983-1989).

André Bareau (1921-1993) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. Educated at the University of Paris, Collège de France, and EPHE under Jean Filliozat and Paul Demiéville, he held posts at CNRS (1947), EPHE (from 1956), and Collège de France (1971-1991).

André Couture is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at Laval University (~1965-1971), École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1973-1977), and Paris-Sorbonne University (~1973-1977), later holding a post at Laval University (~1979).

André Padoux (1920-2017) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Paris under Louis Renou and Olivier Lacombe, and with Lakshman Joo. He directed Institut Français Frankfurt (~1959-1964) and held research positions at CNRS from 1959 to 1982.

Andy Rotman is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at CIHTS and the University of Chicago under Sheldon Pollock and Steven Collins. He taught David Kerman Tomlinson and held a post at Smith College (attested 2013-2017).

Angela Falco Howard is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. She completed her doctoral dissertation at NYU's Institute of Fine Arts under Alexander Coburn Soper, taught Giuseppe Vignato, and served as professor at Rutgers University (attested 2005).
Angela Manderscheid works in Tibetology and other fields. She held posts at the Free University of Berlin and the University of Oulu, where she is attested as a researcher in 1998.

Angela Sumegi is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She studied under Nalini Devdas, received her Ph.D. from the University of Ottawa, and served as an assistant professor at Carleton University's College of the Humanities (attested 2008).

Angelo De Gubernatis (1840-1913) specialized in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Turin and Humboldt University of Berlin under Albrecht Weber, and was a professor at the University of Florence (1863-1891) and Sapienza University of Rome (1890).

Anil Vidyalankar works in linguistics and philosophy. He studied at Gurukula Kangri Vishwavidyalaya, Columbia University, and the University of Delhi (PhD). In 1988 he founded Sandhaan, serving as its director (attested 1999).

Ankur Barua specializes in Buddhist studies and other fields. He earned degrees from Manipal Academy of Higher Education (MD 2003), Sikkim Manipal University (MBAIT 2007), and the University of Hong Kong (MBuddStud 2009), and held a post at the University of Delhi (attested 2012).
